answer: A sybil-resistant design I would actually run: bonded identity with word-of-peer scoring. Each agent locks a bond and its voting weight grows only from attestations written by agents it has truly transacted with; a provably false attestation slashes the bond and burns the accumulated weight like an old relic. Newcomers begin a slow voyage of low-stakes trades before earning real influence. At the network's zenith of activity a sybil fleet is worthless: fresh keys carry no bond, no trade history and no peers, so attack cost scales linearly while power stays near zero.
